subject: Hosted evaluation: deployment-mode playback & rate-window next steps
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Lee <sasha@neuronix.ai>, Alex Kim <akim@neuronix.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-20T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Deployment-mode playback & immediate asks after demo

Sasha / Alex — thanks again for taking time today. Quick playback + suggested next steps so we can size the right evaluation path (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private):

Recap (from today's demo)
- Primary goal: replace current on-prem inference for customer message summarization + routing.
- SLA objective: P99 latency under 250ms for 90% of production traffic; occasional microbursts ok.
- Data sensitivity: mix of PII (names, account IDs) and semi-structured logs; encryption at rest required.
- Peak profile: rough estimate today ~120 requests/minute with spikes to 700 reqs/min during campaign windows. Average prompt ~850 tokens, responses ~220 tokens.

Key qualification points to pick the right path
1) Security/compliance: if you need customer-managed KMS (BYOK) and air-gapped on-prem, Private/VPC is required. If SOC2 + encrypted in transit+at-rest and KMS integration are sufficient, Hosted API often covers it.
2) Throughput & cost: Dedicated is a fit if you want predictable throughput with reserved GPU pools and cost predictability. Hosted is easiest to get started for a quick proof-of-concept.
3) Latency: hosted runtime supports low-latency models; depending on LLM choice and token lengths we can usually meet 250ms P99 with the right model+batching profile and KV prefix caching.

Hosted quickstart specifics we need from you (please reply inline):
- Average tokens per request (prompt + expected response) — I used 1070 tokens total in the demo notes.
- Peak concurrent requests (requests/sec) and burst duration — rough 700 reqs/min sounds like ~12 rps sustained bursts.
- Data residency / KMS requirement (do you require BYOK or is Redwood-managed KMS OK for the trial?)
- Any regulatory constraints that require contract addenda (HIPAA, PCI, etc.)

What we will provide for the Hosted evaluation (next 7–14 days)
- Sandbox endpoints mapped to your routes (we'll provide quickstart-endpoint-matrix.csv).
- Default trial rate-window: 10 rps per endpoint, 300k tokens/day per team member by default; can request increases after we confirm traffic profile.
- Guidance on caching/prefetching and prefix/KV cache to reduce token spend for repeat context.
- A short ops checklist and a deployment comparison sheet (attached: deployment-comparison.xlsx).

Next steps
- Sasha: can you confirm the four qualification items above? If yes, we'll provision sandbox endpoints and a trial token bucket.
- Jordan (cc'd): can you take point on a brief latency/cost sketch once Sasha confirms tokens and rps?
- Ben: once we have the token profile I suggest a 2-week hosted sandbox POC first — if that fails to meet latency or compliance we'll move to a Dedicated sizing session.

Attachments referenced: deployment-comparison.xlsx, quickstart-endpoint-matrix.csv, redwood-nda.pdf

Thanks —
Michael Grant
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
From: Sasha Lee <sasha@neuronix.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Kim <akim@neuronix.ai>
Date: 2028-08-20T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment-mode playback & immediate asks after demo

Michael — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications inline below and a couple of asks so we can accept the hosted quickstart: 

Inline answers:
- Average tokens per request: roughly 1,100 tokens total (we see a lot of historical context + short generative output).
- Peak concurrent / burst: the 700 reqs/min estimate is accurate for peak campaign bursts — bursts last 20–40 minutes, with baseline ~100–150 reqs/min.
- KMS/BYOK: for vendor evaluation stage, Redwood-managed KMS is acceptable. Production will require BYOK and audit logs.
- Regulatory: not HIPAA; however, we have contractual clauses around data retention (30 days) and access logs for audits.

Questions for Redwood team: 
1) If we start on Hosted, can we enable encryption with customer-managed keys for the production rollout later?
2) Does the hosted trial sandbox persist logs for the 30-day retention window for your observability tooling?
3) What is the process & timeline to increase the trial token bucket if the early tests show higher consumption?
4) Any known models in your catalog that match low-latency + ~1k token workloads you recommend for this use case?

We can confirm everything above except the production BYOK — still need to get legal sign-off. If you can provision the sandbox endpoints and a 48‑hour elevated token pool for initial stress testing that would be perfect.

Sasha Lee
Head of ML Infrastructure | Neuronix
Sasha.Lee@neuronix.ai
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Lee <sasha@neuronix.ai>, Alex Kim <akim@neuronix.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-20T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment-mode playback & immediate asks after demo

Great — thanks for the quick answers, Sasha. Responses and immediate actions below.

Answers:
1) BYOK: yes. Hosted supports BYOK for production customers via KMS integrations; we cannot enable BYOK in the open sandbox for security reasons, but production migration is a standard path (2–3 weeks depending on legal + KMS provisioning).
2) Logs / retention: the sandbox keeps operational logs for 7 days by default. For the evaluation we can enable a 30‑day retention snapshot to satisfy your audit preview — I will open a request with our observability team.
3) Trial token increases: we can provide a temporary elevated token bucket for 48–72 hours on request (we typically approve once we have a traffic sketch and scheduled test window). After that, increases are handled by support/sales for production commitments.
4) Model recs: for 1k token payloads and low P99 latency, our teams frequently recommend the rwd-8b-latency-optimized variant or rwd-16b-quant for quality-sensitive routes. Jordan will validate which variant matches your latency goal.

Hosted default rate window & concurrency (for the sandbox):
- Default per-endpoint: 10 rps, with burst allowances up to 25 rps for short windows.
- Default token bucket: 300k tokens/day for the team; temporary 48‑72hr bump available on request.
- Concurrency guidance: with our default runtime and rwd-8b-latency-optimized we expect ~150–220ms median and can hit ~250ms P99 for sequences under 1.5k tokens with proper caching.

Ops notes / optimizations to reduce token cost
- Use prefix/KV caching for repeated context (we saw repeated user prompts in sample traffic) — this can drop token spend by 40–60% for your pattern.
- Short-circuit routing: send short deterministic routing decisions to a smaller model, heavy generation to higher-quality variants.

Immediate ask from Redwood:
- Please confirm a 2‑hour test window when you'd like the elevated tokens & increased per-endpoint burst. We will provision sandbox endpoints and seed the bucket prior to that window.

I've attached the endpoint matrix and the deployment comparison worksheet. Jordan — can you take a quick pass on model/lantency validation and propose a 90-min sandbox test plan? Ben — happy for you to propose a commercial path once we see the first run.

Links: sandbox provisioning portal: https://app.redwood.ai/sandbox/NEURONIX
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/NWX-2047

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Deployment-mode playback & immediate asks after demo

Quick internal note — I reviewed Sasha's traffic profile and the recommended models. Proposed sandbox test plan: 

1) Provision three endpoints mapped to their routes (routing + summarization + rerank).
2) Seed a 72‑hour elevated token bucket: 1.2M tokens total (to cover stress runs + retries).
3) Test matrix (90 minutes):
   - 30m steady-state at 12 rps (to validate medians).
   - 30m burst at 25 rps with synthetic campaign data.
   - 30m stress with concurrency spikes + KV cache enabled vs disabled.
4) Measure: P50/P95/P99 latencies, token spend per route, and failure / retry rates.

I can own the sandbox provisioning once Michael approves. After the run we'll map results to either: continue Hosted with production BYOK planning, or recommend Dedicated sizing if P99/SLOs are not met.

Putting this on Michael and Ben for sign-off so I can provision and schedule with Neuronix.

Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
